**Priority:** P2 (Taco batch 2026-10-17, items 5, 6, 7)  
**Queue item:** (none in this PR — Architect may add a master-plan line after land; do not edit `JARVIS_MASTER_PLAN.md` here)

## Problem

Verified in `development` @ `3f17c3d8`:

1. **No "Update".** `installer/windows/Jarvis.iss::InitializeWizard` shows the existing-install page with "Upgrade to ANZU X (recommended)" only when the installer is newer (`ExistingVersionRelation > 0`), otherwise "Repair"; plus Reinstall / Semi-clean / Clean. There is no option to bring **installed components** (models, voices) up to date without reinstalling.
2. **Default model is old and heavy, and there are two 9Bs.** `config/default.json` uses profile `fast` (`Qwen3.5-9B-abliterated-Q6_K.gguf`, `backend/app/inference/profiles.py`), whose fallback is `bootstrap` = **Ornith 1.5 9B Q4_K_M**, which release installers already ship (`Jarvis.iss:147` payload `models\bootstrap\Ornith-1.5-9B-Q4_K_M.gguf`, staged by `installer/windows/stage-bootstrap-model.ps1` / `build-installer.ps1:57`; `bootstrap.ps1::Ensure-BootstrapGguf` downloads it when missing). `dl_localllm` → `bootstrap.ps1` additionally downloads Abiray **Q8_0 + Q6_K**. Taco wants the Defiant-Fable 9B at Q4/Q3. `lmstudio_graded_profiles.json` already matches `["Qwen3.5-9B", "Defiant", "Q4"]` as "Cheap coding 9B".
3. **"New installs only" has no mechanism.** `config.py::load_settings` deep-merges `data_dir()/settings.json` **over** `config/default.json`; an install whose `settings.json` has no `inference.profile` silently follows whatever `default.json` says, so changing the default would switch existing installs.
4. **RFC-0063 benchmark gate.** `default_candidates.py::ModelCandidate` says "A candidate must win the local Jarvis benchmark before it can be promoted to the default runtime" (`benchmark_required = True`), but nothing enforces or records it.
5. **Model pinned forever.** `InferenceSettings` has no idle unload; the managed llama-server and LM Studio instances stay resident; and `inference/gpu_prefer.py::ensure_ollama_gpu` warms every ANZU-started Ollama model (incl. the Umi persona brain via `ollama_runtime.ensure_local_ollama`) with `keep_alive: "24h"`, competing with `anzu-coder-27b` for VRAM.
6. **The orchestrator default and its idle restore are hard-wired to Ornith.** `inference/profile_roles.py::default_orchestrator_profile_name()` returns `"ornith_9b"` and `orchestrator_profile_names()` returns `("ornith_9b", "bootstrap")`. `inference/model_escalation.py::schedule_orchestrator_restore` (called after every chat turn from `agent/loop.py` and after every visible switch to a heavy model) sleeps `orchestrator_idle_seconds` (default 120 s) and then calls `MANAGER.load(app, "ornith_9b")` whenever the loaded profile is not an orchestrator profile; any exception is swallowed (`except Exception: return`). `effective_answer_profile_name` also falls back to `ornith_9b`. With a Fable-only fresh install this either fails silently (no `Ornith-1.5-9B-Q8_0.gguf`) or swaps the worker away from `fable_9b`, and it is a second reload path racing this RFC's 9B reload.
7. **Installed options are indistinguishable.** The `[Tasks]` checklist (`dl_kokoro`, `dl_personavoices`, `dl_whisper`, `dl_voicestudio`, `dl_pockettts`, `dl_umi_brain`, `dl_localllm`, `dl_expert27b`, voice-pack tasks) is `checkedonce` regardless of what is on disk, with no notion of a newer replacement.

**Verified external fact (2026-10-20, Hugging Face listing):** the GGUF repo is `DavidAU/Qwen3.5-9B-The-Defiant-Fable-Uncensored-Heretic-NEO-IMATRIX-MAX-MTP-GGUF`; regular quants include `…-NEO-MAX-Q4_K_S.gguf` (≈6.10 GB), `…-Q4_K_M.gguf` (≈6.36 GB), `…-IQ4_XS.gguf` (≈5.96 GB), `…-IQ3_M.gguf` (≈5.23 GB); MTP variants exist. The LM Studio model key Taco uses (`qwen3.5-9b-defiant-fable-uncensored`) is taken from the owner's message and must be confirmed against `lms ls` on Taco's PC (S1).

## Decision

Ship **one RFC with four implement slices** (one named model each, **fast off**). #648/#649 are already on `development`.

### Default model (normative)

- New profile `fable_9b` in `profiles.py` (existing `fast`, `balanced`, `bootstrap`, `ornith_9b`, `expert` and Abiray entries are **kept**, not deleted): repo above, file **Q4_K_S regular** (not MTP — MTP needs temp ≤1 and has acceptance caveats), fallback **IQ3_M** when free VRAM < 7 GB or disk < 8 GB. Repo commit SHA + file SHA256 pinned in `installer/windows/model-catalog.json` at implement time (same pinned-revision + SHA pattern as `runtime_install.py` uses for its downloads); download verified before the profile is selectable.
- **RFC-0063 gate (D2 #4).** `default_candidates.py` gains `benchmark_evidence: str` on `ModelCandidate` and `promotable_default(candidate, incumbent) -> bool`: true only if `benchmark_required` is false, or `benchmark_evidence` names a committed report produced by `inference/harness.py::run_harness` (same report shape as `load_last_report()`) whose score is ≥ the incumbent's on the same machine. S1 runs the harness for the Fable 9B Q4_K_S and the incumbent (`fast`, falling back to Ornith `bootstrap`) on Taco's PC and commits `docs/rfcs/assets/0228-fable-9b-benchmark.json`. The Fable candidate is admitted as default **only** through `promotable_default`; if it loses, S1 stops and reports to the Architect (no default change).
- **Ornith decision (Architect, normative; D2 #5).** Fresh installs ship and use **one** default 9B: the Fable 9B Q4_K_S **replaces** Ornith 1.5 9B Q4_K_M as the installer payload (`Jarvis.iss` payload line, copied only per "Payload copy rule" below; `stage-bootstrap-model.ps1`, `build-installer.ps1`) and as `bootstrap.ps1`'s missing-model download, so a fresh install never downloads a second ~6 GB 9B. If LM Studio is already serving the Fable 9B at install / first run (`installer/windows/detect-lmstudio-model.ps1` probes `http://127.0.0.1:1234/api/v1/models`, else `lms ls`), Setup attaches to it (backend `lmstudio`, port 1234, `remote_model` = that key) and copies/downloads **no** 9B at all; the owner is told which was chosen. Existing installs that have Ornith **keep** it and the `bootstrap` / `ornith_9b` profiles; the installer shows it as `(can be updated to > Qwen3.5 9B Defiant-Fable Q4)`.
- **"New installs only" mechanism (D2 #3).**
  - *Fresh install:* `bootstrap.ps1` (and, as a safety net, the first `load_settings()` that finds no `settings.json`) writes an explicit `inference` block into `data_dir()/settings.json`: `profile: "fable_9b"` (or the LM Studio attach settings above), plus marker `migrations: ["0228_profile_pinned"]`.
  - *Existing install (migration, runs before the default changes):* Inno `PrepareToInstall` (before files are copied) runs `installer/windows/pin-effective-profile.ps1`, which reads the **old** `{app}\config\default.json` and `settings.json`, and writes the currently effective `inference.profile` (and `backend`/`host`/`port`/`remote_model` when absent) into `settings.json` with the marker. Backend safety net in `config.py::load_settings`: if `settings.json` exists, lacks `inference.profile` and lacks the marker, pin `LEGACY_DEFAULT_PROFILE = "fast"` (the `default.json` value before this RFC) and add the marker. Only after both exist does `config/default.json` change to `"profile": "fable_9b"`.
  - Result: `default.json`'s profile is never the effective profile of any install that existed before this change.
- **Payload copy rule (D2 re-review #2).** Inno copies `[Files]` on Upgrade, Repair, Reinstall and (S3) Update too, so the Fable payload line must never copy unconditionally. The line is `Source: "payload\models\bootstrap\<Fable Q4_K_S file>"; DestDir: "{app}\models\bootstrap"; Flags: ignoreversion; Check: ShouldCopyDefault9BPayload`, and `ShouldCopyDefault9BPayload` (S1, `[Code]`) is true **only** when LM Studio is not already serving Fable **and** one of:
  - fresh install (`not ExistingInstallDetected`), or Clean reinstall (models wiped; tested through a named helper `ExistingActionIsClean`, not a raw page index, so S3's new Update entry cannot shift it);
  - existing install whose pinned profile (written by `pin-effective-profile.ps1` in `PrepareToInstall` to `{tmp}\pinned-profile.txt`) is already `fable_9b` and the Fable file is missing under `{app}\models\bootstrap` (repair of its own default);
  - (added by S3) the owner opted in to the successor: `Default9BSuccessorOptedIn` = the `(can be updated to > Qwen3.5 9B Defiant-Fable Q4)` task ticked, or `/UPGRADEMODELS` names `fable_9b`.
  Upgrade / Repair / Reinstall / Semi-clean / Update of an Ornith or Abiray install with the successor unticked therefore copies **no** Fable file. The same rule gates `bootstrap.ps1`'s download: it never fetches Fable on an existing install unless it was opted in (`-UpgradeModels fable_9b`) or that install's own pinned profile is `fable_9b`.

### Idle unload + reload (normative)

Terms are RFC-0225's: **reload** = loading a model into a listening engine (this RFC); **revive** / **respawn** = RFC-0225. `prepare_engine_for()` (RFC-0225 S3) is the single entry; this RFC registers the idle state through `engine_coexistence.note_idle_unload()` so RFC-0225 never treats an idle-unloaded engine as dead or foreign, and supplies the reload routine `prepare_engine_for` delegates to. Single-flight is RFC-0225's (no double reload).

- `InferenceSettings.idle_unload_seconds` (default **900**, `0` = pinned; range 0–86400). Applies to the **worker** model only; the front lane (`front_responder.resident`) is unchanged.
- Managed llama-server: after `idle_unload_seconds` with no request lease held and no task running, `MANAGER.unload()`; next request transparently reloads (same profile/context), with the existing "Loading model…" HUD state and elapsed timer.
- LM Studio selected engine, **managed mode off** (default): pass a native TTL when the installed LM Studio supports it (`lms load --ttl` / REST `ttl`), else ANZU's own timer calls `/api/v1/models/unload` for the instance it loaded; on demand ANZU reloads through `lmstudio_context`/`ensure_local_lmstudio`. "The instance it loaded" is an entry in the RFC-0225 engine ledger's `anzu_loads` section (the S2 reload routine calls `engine_coexistence.record_anzu_load()` after each verified load, and `forget_anzu_load()` after each verified unload). ANZU never unloads LM Studio instances it did not load.
- LM Studio selected engine, **managed mode on** (RFC-0225 `is_managed()`; consent asked once in the RFC-0225 S4 prompt / Model page, remembered, revocable): ANZU may load, unload and reload **any** instance of the selected model(s) on that LM Studio, including instances the owner loaded himself (e.g. Taco's 9B on :1234). It applies `idle_unload_seconds` to them, preferring LM Studio's native TTL (re-load the instance with `ttl` via REST / `lms load --ttl`, same model key + context as the owner's instance) and otherwise its own timer + `/api/v1/models/unload`; on the next request it reloads via the LM Studio API / `lms load` with the recorded model key and context, then answers. Managed mode never stops the LM Studio server or app.
- **Ollama keep-alive (D2 #7, per-engine rule).** Every ANZU-originated Ollama load/warm (`gpu_prefer.ensure_ollama_gpu`, chat/generate requests ANZU sends) uses `keep_alive = f"{idle_unload_seconds}s"`, and `"-1"` (pinned) when `idle_unload_seconds == 0`; the hard-coded `"24h"` is removed from that call. **The Umi persona brain is not an exception:** it follows the same value, and the next Umi turn reloads it through the existing `ensure_local_ollama` path in `api/named_personas.py`. Ollama models ANZU did not load (Taco's `anzu-coder-27b` started from his shell) are never sent a `keep_alive` by the idle timer; requests ANZU routes to them carry the same derived `keep_alive`, which is the only effect.
- **VRAM yielding for `anzu-coder-27b`.** The VRAM gate itself is RFC-0225 S3 (`prepare_engine_for` step 5): an **ANZU-loaded** 9B (the managed llama-server worker, or an LM Studio instance in `anzu_loads`) is unloaded in any mode with one owner line; an **owner-loaded** 9B is unloaded only with managed mode on, and with managed mode off the request fails visibly naming the owner-loaded 9B. This RFC adds the re-warm through the single 9B re-warm coordinator below: once the 27B has left VRAM (its `keep_alive` = `idle_unload_seconds` expired and Ollama `/api/ps` no longer lists it; never earlier, see the coordinator rule), ANZU reloads whichever 9B the gate unloaded (ANZU-loaded: any mode; owner-loaded: managed mode on only, with the recorded key + context) so ordinary chat is warm again, one owner line "Reloaded the 9B.".

### Orchestrator default + one 9B re-warm path (normative; D2 re-review #1, owned by S2)

- **Default follows the saved / selected 9B, derived from the profile catalogue (D2 second re-review #2).** `profile_roles.py`: `fable_9b` joins `_ORCHESTRATOR` (role `orchestrator`, tier 1) and `orchestrator_profile_names()` returns `("fable_9b", "ornith_9b", "bootstrap")`. There is **no hand-written 9B list**. Instead:
  - `catalog_profile(name) -> ModelProfile | None` looks the name up **without fallback** in `profiles.declared_profiles()`, `model_discovery.resolve_discovered_profile`, `qwen38_9b_profile()` and `qwen38_27b_heretic_profile()`. `resolve_profile()` is deliberately not used, because it silently maps unknown names to `bootstrap` / `balanced`.
  - `profile_param_billions(profile) -> float | None` parses the catalogue `alias` with `(?<![\w.])(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)[Bb](?![a-z])` (first match). On `development` this gives `bootstrap` / `ornith_9b` "Ornith-1.5-9B" → 9, `fast` / `balanced` / `quality` "Qwen3.5-9B" → 9, `expert` "Qwen3.5-27B" → 27, `ornith_35b` "Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B" → 35 (the `A3B` is skipped by the look-behind), `front_2b` / `front_4b` → 2 / 4, `qwen38_9b` → 9, `qwen38_27b_heretic` → 27, a `local_gguf` profile → from its file-stem alias, and `fable_9b` (S1 alias "Qwen3.5-9B-Defiant-Fable") → 9.
  - `is_nine_b_worker(profile)` is `7 <= profile_param_billions(profile) <= 10`.
  - `default_orchestrator_profile_name(settings=None) -> str | None` (settings re-read with `load_settings()` when not passed) returns, for **every** saved profile:
    - saved profile in the catalogue and `is_nine_b_worker` → that name: `fable_9b` (fresh install), `bootstrap` / `ornith_9b` (kept Ornith), `fast`, `balanced` and `quality` (kept Abiray; `balanced` and `quality` are the Abiray Q8_0 profiles), `qwen38_9b`, or a 9B `local_gguf`;
    - LM Studio attach (backend `lmstudio`, no profile) → the selected `settings.inference.remote_model`;
    - saved profile in the catalogue but not a 9B worker (`expert`, `ornith_35b`, `qwen38_27b_heretic`, `front_*`) → `None`, meaning the owner chose that model as the worker, so there is no restore target;
    - saved name not in the catalogue (unknown / renamed) → `None`, plus one `orchestrator_restore_skipped reason=unknown_profile name=<n>` log line per process (no per-turn owner line).
  - `None` means `NINE_B_REWARM` does nothing for the orchestrator trigger and **the loaded model is kept**. No swap happens and no "missing file" line is shown on every turn. The literal `"ornith_9b"` is never returned unconditionally. `infer_runtime_role_and_tier` keeps every existing mapping (`tests/test_rfc0115_routing.py` unchanged).
- **One coordinator.** New `backend/app/inference/rewarm.py::NINE_B_REWARM` is the only code that reloads the 9B on a timer. It owns one `asyncio.Lock` and at most one pending timer. Two triggers feed it: `model_escalation.schedule_orchestrator_restore` (after a heavy turn, delay `orchestrator_idle_seconds`) and the 27B-idle re-warm above. A new schedule keeps the earlier due time; it never starts a second timer.
- **A 9B the VRAM gate unloaded is re-warmed only by the 27B-idle trigger (D2 second re-review #1).** When the RFC-0225 gate unloads a 9B to make room for a large model, it records `engine_coexistence.note_gate_unload(nine_b=<target>, heavy=<engine, model>)` (an RFC-0225 S3 hook, next to `note_idle_unload`). `NINE_B_REWARM` reads it through `engine_coexistence.gate_unloaded()` and clears it with `clear_gate_unload()`. While that marker is set:
  - the orchestrator trigger is a **no-op** (dropped, not deferred);
  - the 27B-idle trigger fires only once the heavy model has **left VRAM**: Ollama `/api/ps` no longer lists it (its `keep_alive` = `idle_unload_seconds` expired), or, for an LM Studio / llama-server heavy model, native inventory shows it unloaded. Until then it re-polls `/api/ps` every 30 s off the event loop.
  - Then exactly one reload of the gate-unloaded 9B runs, with one owner line `engine_coexistence.owner_line("Reloaded the 9B.")` (RFC-0225 "Owner-line surfaces": an `engine_notice` frame rendered and spoken by the HUD `EngineNotices` consumer), and the marker is cleared.
  - A new request for the heavy model while waiting keeps it resident and the wait continues. A **chat request for the 9B while the 27B is resident** goes through `prepare_engine_for` and is decided by **RFC-0225 step 6 (reverse direction)**, never by the timer. Measured free VRAM fits the 9B → it loads and nothing is unloaded. Short and the 27B is ANZU-loaded → the 27B is unloaded (verified), `clear_gate_unload()`, the 9B loads through the same prepare/reload path, and one owner line is emitted. Short and the 27B is owner-loaded, or the unload fails / VRAM stays short → explicit error line, no blind load. Meanwhile the resident 2B front lane answers the turn. Any successful 9B load clears the marker, so the pending 27B-idle trigger then finds nothing to do and the timer never reloads the 9B a second time.
  - **Decision (Architect): defer rather than force-unload the 27B.**
    - *VRAM:* both choices avoid oversubscription. Deferring never holds two large models at once, and it never evicts a model ANZU just loaded for an active coding session.
    - *Latency:* force-unloading the 27B at 120 s would make the next coding request (bursty, minutes apart) pay a ~12 GB reload, then evict the 9B again through the gate. That ping-pong costs two large loads per coding burst. Deferring costs at most one 9B reload (the existing "Loading model…" state, done by the RFC-0225 step 6 reverse rule while the 2B front lane answers) on the first chat turn after a coding burst, and only when that turn arrives before the 27B idles out.
    - The 27B is still never held longer than `idle_unload_seconds` (15 min default).
  - **Last guard:** the coordinator measures free VRAM (RFC-0225 `vram.py`) before any timer reload and skips the reload if free < the 9B requirement + 1 GB. So a restore never loads the 9B while a resident model leaves no room, whoever loaded that model.
- **`schedule_orchestrator_restore` stops calling `MANAGER.load` itself.** It calls `NINE_B_REWARM.schedule(reason="orchestrator_restore", delay=orchestrator_idle_seconds(app))`. On fire, under the lock, the coordinator re-reads settings, resolves the target with `default_orchestrator_profile_name()`, and:
  - target already loaded → no-op;
  - target is `None` (non-9B or unknown saved profile) → no-op, loaded model kept;
  - a gate-unload marker is set → no-op (see above);
  - the 9B was unloaded by the idle timer (`engine_coexistence.idle_unloaded()` true, timestamp `unloaded_idle_at`) → no-op; it is **never** reloaded by a timer, only by the next request through `prepare_engine_for` (the S2 idle unload also cancels any pending re-warm);
  - a request lease is held → waits for it (same bound as the idle timer);
  - target weights missing → no swap away from the loaded model, and one owner line `engine_coexistence.owner_line("Couldn't switch back to <target>: its model file is missing.", level="error", engine_id=…)` plus the RFC-0225 `engines:<engine_id>` health-rail item (no silent `return`);
  - otherwise reloads through the **same** S2 reload routine (`prepare_engine_for` → reload: `MANAGER.load(app, target)` for the managed llama-server, the `lmstudio_server` reload routine for LM Studio), so `prepare_engine_for`'s single-flight joins it with any concurrent on-demand reload; a failure is surfaced with the engine error, never swallowed and never retried in a loop.
- `effective_answer_profile_name` falls back to `default_orchestrator_profile_name()` (the saved 9B), then to the loaded profile, then to the saved profile name, never to `ornith_9b`. `agent/loop.py` is not edited (it keeps calling `schedule_orchestrator_restore`).
- **Owner-visible lines:** every line in this RFC ("Reloaded the 9B.", "Couldn't switch back to …", every failed unload / reload) goes through RFC-0225's `engine_coexistence.owner_line()` and nothing else. Every call uses the default title "Local engines": none of them passes RFC-0225's optional `title` parameter, and RFC-0225's static test `test_rfc0225_and_rfc0228_lines_use_default_title` covers RFC-0228's modules. That publishes an `engine_notice` frame on `OWNER_CHAT_CHANNEL`, which the HUD `EngineNotices` consumer (RFC-0225 S3) shows as a chip and speaks when speak-replies is on, plus the task copy (`engine_notice` + `chat_tts`) when a turn is known. `publish_owner_text` is never used for these lines, because its channel has no client on `development`. Failures also appear on the HUD health rail as the per-engine `engines:<engine_id>` self-check item; exactly one line per unload-for-VRAM (RFC-0225) and per re-warm reload; idle unloads are logged and shown in the HUD model state ("unloaded (idle) for 12 min", consumed by RFC-0229 S2), not announced. Every failed unload/reload is surfaced to the owner with the LM Studio/Ollama error; never swallowed, never retried silently in a loop.
- Never unload during an active stream, tool loop or task stage; the timer resets on every lease.

### Installer Update + installed state (normative)

1. **"Update" option** on the existing-install page, inserted as a new first-class entry: "&Update ANZU — keep everything, refresh the app and bring installed models and voices up to date". Existing entries (Upgrade/Repair primary, Reinstall, Semi-clean, Clean) are **kept with their current text and behaviour**; when the installer is newer, Upgrade stays the default selection; when versions match, Update becomes the default selection (Repair stays available).
2. **Update never auto-switches the model (D2 #1).** Update = Upgrade/Repair file copy + refresh of **installed** components at their current version (re-verify, repair missing files). The saved profile (`settings.json`, pinned per the mechanism above) and the HUD slots (`data_dir()/hud/model-selector.json`, RFC-0227 S3) are kept byte-identical. A successor is downloaded **only** when the owner ticks its `(can be updated to > …)` task (rule 4); after it verifies, the profile switches to it **only because the owner opted in through that tick**, and the old files and profile are kept so slots that reference them keep working. Unticked → nothing downloaded, nothing switched.
3. **Installed detection** (run before `wpSelectTasks` and **never blocking**: S3 launches its marker-only check, file-exists and version reads with no hashing, from `InitializeWizard` with the non-blocking mechanism in "When the check runs" (`ewNoWait`, result file, inline indicator, timer, apply-once, kill, visible fallback); S4 adds hashing to the same run) from a shared manifest `installer/windows/model-catalog.json` (component id → files/markers, version, GPU/RAM/disk profile, `superseded_by`, pinned repo commit + SHA256) evaluated by `installer/windows/installed-components.ps1` (also usable by the backend). Inno reads its JSON result.
4. **Greyed tasks:** already-installed, up-to-date components are shown checked + disabled with suffix "(installed)". Installed-but-outdated components with a successor whose VRAM, RAM and disk needs are each within **±25 %** (or lower) of the installed one are shown **unchecked** and enabled, labelled `(can be updated to > <successor display name>)`; ticking it is the owner's opt-in (rule 2).
5. Fresh installs: no greying; default selections as RFC-0196 (27B unchecked); single default 9B per the Ornith decision.
6. Silent mode (`/VERYSILENT`) supports `/UPDATE` with the same semantics (no successor unless `/UPGRADEMODELS=<ids>` names it).
7. The `dl_localllm` description changes to the Defiant-Fable 9B; existing Abiray 9B and Ornith 9B installs are "outdated" with successor `fable_9b` (similar profile) → labelled per rule 4.

### Skip unchanged bundled assets (normative; Taco 2026-10-20, owned by S4)

**Manifest (hashes only from here).** On `development` there is no single model manifest. The expected hashes and sizes sit inline in scripts: `installer/windows/stage-front-model.ps1:42` (`$ExpectedSha` + `$ExpectedBytes` for the 2B front GGUF, build-time staging), and `bootstrap.ps1::Ensure-Front2bGguf` (`$expectedBytes = 1280835840`, size only, no hash). `Ensure-BootstrapGguf` accepts any non-empty file. The batch's manifest is **`installer/windows/model-catalog.json`**, created by S3 (component id → files/markers, version, resource profile, `superseded_by`, pinned commit + SHA256). S4 extends every file entry with `size` (bytes) and `sha256` (lower-case hex), plus `superseded_files[]` (`size`, `sha256`, `version`) for the outdated versions S3 already names. It also moves the two inline constants into the catalogue: `stage-front-model.ps1` and `bootstrap.ps1` read them from it, and a test keeps them from drifting. Hashes are never computed from "whatever is on disk" or guessed at runtime; a component without a catalogue `sha256` is never classified (a) and keeps today's behaviour.

**One shared helper.** The installer runs on PowerShell scripts that Inno launches (`bootstrap.ps1`, and S3's `installed-components.ps1`, whose JSON Inno already reads). So the check lives in **`installer/windows/asset-state.ps1`** (new, dot-sourced), with `Get-AnzuAssetState -Catalog <path> -Root <app> -Component <id> [-HashCachePath] [-HashTimeoutSeconds 900] [-ProgressPath]`. It is called by:
- `installed-components.ps1`, which Inno starts **before the Select Tasks page** (see "When the check runs" below; not in `PrepareToInstall`, which runs after the owner has already submitted the task list). It writes `{tmp}\asset-state.json` (per component: `state`, `files[]`, `message`). That file drives the checklist labels and pre-ticks on `wpSelectTasks`, and `Preparing` and the `[Files]` `Check:` lookups reuse the same file without re-running the check;
- `bootstrap.ps1` (the updater path: `-Update`, and fresh-install downloads), before every model download in `Ensure-*`. It reuses the same hash cache, so files Setup just verified are not hashed again.

`[Code]` contains **no** size or hash logic: it reads the JSON (`AssetNeedsCopy('<component>', '<destPath>')` = state is `missing`, `damaged` or `hash-failed`; with no usable JSON, i.e. the fallback, it is `not FileExists(destPath)`, S1's check). Payload model lines carry `Check: AssetNeedsCopy('<component>', ExpandConstant('{app}\models\…\<file>'))`, combined with existing Checks by `and`. **Wildcard payloads (D2 sixth review #4).** A `Source:` with `*` has no single `<file>`, so its `destPath` is the component's version marker `{app}\<DestDir>\.anzu-asset-version.json`, and `AssetNeedsCopy` memoises its result per component on the first call, so the per-file evaluation of a wildcard entry can't change half-way through the copy. See "Version marker for wildcard payloads" below.

**States per component (all files must agree):**
- **(a) present and unchanged.** Every file exists, its size equals the catalogue `size`, **then** its SHA-256 equals the catalogue `sha256`. The download and the payload copy are skipped. The checklist row is **pre-checked** and its label is **prefixed** `(already installed) `. S3's grey-out stays: the row is still disabled, so unticking can't delete a verified file. bootstrap logs `Write-Skip "<name> (already installed)"`.
- **(b) present but outdated.** Size + hash match a `superseded_files` entry → S3's existing `(can be updated to > <successor>)` behaviour, **unchanged** (unchecked, enabled, opt-in, `ShouldCopyDefault9BPayload` rules). Nothing is downloaded unless ticked.
- **(c) missing.** Download / copy as today.
- **damaged** (size matches nothing, or size matches but the hash matches nothing): treated as (c), with the visible line "<name> is damaged; downloading it again." Not a fourth checkbox state.
- **hash-failed** (I/O error, file locked, or hashing exceeded `-HashTimeoutSeconds`): treated as (c), with the visible line "Couldn't verify <name> (<error>); downloading it again." **Never silent:** the line is shown in the wizard (progress page and, in `CurStepChanged(ssPostInstall)`, the Finished-page summary read from `{tmp}\asset-state.json`), and written to `{app}\logs\installer-assets.log` and the Inno Setup log. bootstrap prints the same line to its log.

**Size first, hash second, cached.** The size check is free; the hash runs only when the size matches the current or a superseded entry. Hashing streams in 4 MiB blocks (`System.Security.Cryptography.SHA256`), off the wizard thread. The cache `{app}\data\installer\asset-hash-cache.json` is keyed on full path (case-normalised) + size + `LastWriteTimeUtc` ticks and stores `sha256` and `hashed_at`. A hit skips hashing; any change to size or mtime is a miss. A corrupt cache file is discarded and rebuilt, with one log line. Clean reinstall removes it along with `data\`.

**When the check runs (D2 fourth re-review #1).** `wpSelectTasks` is drawn before Ready and Preparing (`Jarvis.iss:759` handles it in `CurPageChanged`; `PrepareToInstall` is `Jarvis.iss:1498`), so the result must exist before the task list is usable. The two candidates per the Inno Setup docs ([event functions](https://jrsoftware.org/ishelp/topic_scriptevents.htm)):
- `InitializeWizard`: "Use this event function to make changes to the wizard or wizard pages at startup". It is the earliest point where the wizard exists, and `ExistingInstallDir` is already known from `InitializeSetup`'s detection (`Jarvis.iss:862–871`). But the wizard isn't on screen yet, so waiting there would block before any window appears, i.e. silently.
- `CurPageChanged(wpSelectTasks)`: "Called after a new wizard page … is shown". This is the last moment before the owner can touch the list, and it is where `Jarvis.iss:759` already sets up that list.

**Decision: start in `InitializeWizard`, gate and apply in `CurPageChanged(wpSelectTasks)`, never wait in either.** **This mechanism is introduced by S3** for its own marker detection (D2 fifth review #5), so nothing ever blocks `InitializeWizard`, not even S3's quick file-exists and version reads. S4 reuses the same launch, result file, indicator, timer, fallback and kill unchanged, and only adds hashing and per-file progress to the run.
- `InitializeWizard` (existing install only): `Exec('powershell.exe', '-NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "{tmp}\installed-components.ps1" -Root "<ExistingInstallDir>" -Out "{tmp}\asset-state.json" -ProgressPath "{tmp}\asset-state.progress" -PidPath "{tmp}\asset-state.pid"', …, SW_HIDE, ewNoWait, ResultCode)`. Per the [Exec docs](https://jrsoftware.org/ishelp/topic_isxfunc_exec.htm), `ewNoWait` returns immediately and gives no exit code, so completion is signalled by the result file. The helper's first action is to write `{tmp}\asset-state.pid` (to `asset-state.pid.partial`, then renamed) with exactly two lines, `pid=<$PID>` and `start=<(Get-Process -Id $PID).StartTime.ToUniversalTime().Ticks>`. Its whole body runs inside `try { … } finally { Remove-Item -LiteralPath $PidPath -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }`, so the helper deletes its own pid file on every exit it controls (success, `{"error"}`, thrown exception). It writes `asset-state.json.partial` and renames it to `asset-state.json` only on success; on its own error it writes `{"error": "<text>"}`. `AssetCheckLaunched: Boolean` is set only when that `Exec` returns True. **Runs from `{tmp}`, never from the install root, and is spared by the force-stop (D2 eighth review #1).**
  - The script ships as `Source: "installed-components.ps1"; DestDir: "{tmp}"; Flags: dontcopy` and is extracted by one more `ExtractTemporaryFile('installed-components.ps1');` line in `ExtractInstallerHelpers` (`Jarvis.iss:891–901`, called from `InitializeSetup` at `:913`). So `-File` names `{tmp}`, and the working directory passed to `Exec` is `{tmp}`.
  - Its command line still contains install-root paths: `-Root "<ExistingInstallDir>"`, and S4's `-HashCachePath "<ExistingInstallDir>\data\installer\asset-hash-cache.json"`. `PrepareToInstall` calls `StopJarvisProcessesForPrepare` at `Jarvis.iss:1511`, before the silent wait, and that runs `force-stop-jarvis.ps1 -InstallRoot <ExistingInstallDir>` (`:1175–1191`). `Test-ProcessUnderInstall` (`force-stop-jarvis.ps1:285–305`) kills any `powershell` whose command line contains `<root>\` (`Test-HaystackUnderRoot`, `:159–167`), so the helper would match.
  - **The spare is bound to this Setup's helper, never to words in a command line (D2 ninth review #1).** `Test-IsProtectedInstallerProcess` is **not** edited; the eighth-review line (`installed-components\.ps1` + `-PidPath` substrings) is dropped, because a stray copy under the root, any script whose arguments name both strings, the root's `python.exe` backend, `-pidpath` and `-PidPathological` all matched it. Instead:
    - **Setup names its own pid file.** In `ForceStopJarvisUnder` (`Jarvis.iss:973–1017`) one statement is added after the `Params :=` assignment (`:994–996`): `if AssetCheckLaunched then Params := Params + ' -SpareAssetPidPath "' + ExpandConstant('{tmp}\asset-state.pid') + '"';`. Existing lines are unchanged, and the elevated retry (`:1013`) reuses `Params`, so it carries the same argument. `AssetCheckLaunched` is declared with the other `[Code]` globals above `:973`.
    - **`force-stop-jarvis.ps1` gains one parameter and one call.** `[string]$SpareAssetPidPath = ""` is appended to the `param(...)` block (`force-stop-jarvis.ps1:14–32`, after `$LogPath`), and one line after `Add-AncestorPids ([int]$PID)` (`:99`) runs `Add-SetupAssetHelperPid $SpareAssetPidPath` when the value is non-empty. That function dot-sources the new `asset-helper-identity.ps1` from `$PSScriptRoot` and calls `Test-AnzuAssetHelperIdentity -PidPath $SpareAssetPidPath`. Only when it returns `ok` is the helper's pid added to `$script:ProtectedPids` (`:50`), which `Test-IsProtectedInstallerProcess` (`:137`) and the kill-map walk (`:590`) already honour. Every other outcome spares nothing and logs one line naming the failed check. A caller that passes no `-SpareAssetPidPath` (the uninstaller, start-up cleanup, every existing path) sees no change at all.
    - **`Test-AnzuAssetHelperIdentity` (new `installer/windows/asset-helper-identity.ps1`) returns `ok` only if every check passes**, in this order:
      1. **Setup temp dir.** `$dir = Split-Path ([IO.Path]::GetFullPath($PidPath))`. The leaf of `$dir` matches `^is-[0-9A-Za-z]+\.tmp$` (Inno Setup's `{tmp}` name), and the parent of `$dir` equals `[IO.Path]::GetTempPath()` with the trailing `\` trimmed (`OrdinalIgnoreCase`). A pid file anywhere else, including under the install root, fails.
      2. **Pid file.** It exists and holds exactly the two lines `pid=<int>` and `start=<int64>` that `installed-components.ps1` writes; anything else fails.
      3. **Pid.** `Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Filter "ProcessId=<pid>"` returns a row.
      4. **Image name.** `Name` equals `powershell.exe` (`OrdinalIgnoreCase`, whole string). `pwsh.exe`, `python.exe` and the rest fail.
      5. **Start time.** `(Get-Process -Id <pid>).StartTime.ToUniversalTime().Ticks` equals `start`. A reused pid fails.
      6. **Exact `-File` path.** `CommandLine` is split into arguments with the Windows rules (`CommandLineToArgvW`, `shell32.dll`, via `Add-Type`), not searched for words. The first argument equal to `-File` (`OrdinalIgnoreCase`, whole token) must be followed by an argument whose `[IO.Path]::GetFullPath` equals `Join-Path $dir 'installed-components.ps1'` (`OrdinalIgnoreCase`). The first argument equal to `-PidPath` (whole token) must be followed by an argument whose full path equals `$PidPath`. `-PidPathological`, a bare `-pidpath` with no value, or a `-File` path anywhere else (a copy under the root, under another `is-*.tmp`) fails.
    - So the only process spared is the one this Setup started from its own `{tmp}`, at the pid and start time it recorded. A backend run of `installed-components.ps1` and every case D2 listed are stopped as before (CoS (b) unchanged). A running helper survives `:1511`, its result appears, and the silent wait reads it. Stopping it remains `KillAssetCheck`'s job alone.
    - `asset-helper-identity.ps1` ships twice: `Source: "asset-helper-identity.ps1"; DestDir: "{tmp}"; Flags: dontcopy` with one more `ExtractTemporaryFile('asset-helper-identity.ps1');` in `ExtractInstallerHelpers` (`:891–901`), so the `{tmp}` copy of `force-stop-jarvis.ps1` that `ResolveForceStopScript` (`:962–971`) prefers finds it next to itself; and inside the existing `installer\*` tree copy for `{app}`. If the file is missing while `-SpareAssetPidPath` is set, nothing is spared and the line `asset-helper-identity.ps1 missing; nothing spared` is logged. The helper may then be stopped, and the silent wait times out into the fallback, which never aborts the install.
  Starting here overlaps the work with the Welcome / License / existing-install pages, and a cache hit (the usual Update case) finishes in under 2 s.
- `CurPageChanged(wpSelectTasks)`: a new `ApplyAssetState` call is added **before** the existing `EnsureSelectAllLayout` / `SyncSelectAll` lines (`Jarvis.iss:759–764`), which are unchanged. If the JSON already exists, the labels and pre-ticks are applied at once. Otherwise the page shows an inline progress indicator, created once in `InitializeWizard` on `WizardForm.SelectTasksPage`: a `TNewProgressBar` plus a `TNewStaticText` reading "Checking installed models… <component> <percent> %". While it runs, `TasksList`, the **Select all box (`TasksSelectAll`, `Jarvis.iss:227`, created at `:747`)** and Next are disabled; Back and Cancel stay enabled. A 250 ms `SetTimer` callback (same `CreateCallback` pattern as the existing glow timer, `Jarvis.iss:244–255`, `:608`) polls `{tmp}\asset-state.progress` and the result file; the UI thread never sleeps. The documented `CreateOutputProgressPage` ([docs](https://jrsoftware.org/ishelp/topic_isxfunc_createoutputprogresspage.htm)) is not used, because its `Show` / `Hide` switches the current page and would re-enter `CurPageChanged`.
- **Applied exactly once.** A global `AssetStateApplied: Boolean` is set the first time the labels and pre-ticks (or the fallback) are applied. Later visits to `wpSelectTasks` (Back → Next) skip `ApplyAssetState` entirely, so the owner's own ticks and unticks are kept. The existing `SyncSelectAll` then re-syncs Select all from the list as it does today.
- On result: labels and pre-ticks are applied per the states below, the indicator hides, and the list, Select all and Next are re-enabled.
- **Clean reinstall** chosen on the existing-install page (`NextButtonClick` on that page, `Jarvis.iss:1096`, after the existing confirmation returns Yes): the background check is **killed** (below) and every model is treated as missing, because the models are being wiped. Going Back and choosing another option starts a fresh check, and `AssetStateApplied` is reset only in that case.
- **Kill on Clean, Cancel and exit (D2 sixth review #1).** `KillAssetCheck` never kills by PID alone:
  - **Only while the helper is running.** It returns at once, starting no process, when (i) `AssetCheckLaunched` is false (fresh install, or the `Exec` failed), (ii) a final result exists (`{tmp}\asset-state.json`, success or `{"error"}`), because the helper has then finished, or (iii) `{tmp}\asset-state.pid` doesn't exist. Case (iii) covers a helper that hasn't written its pid file yet (a timeout while PowerShell is still starting) and one that already exited and deleted it. Setup logs `asset check: no pid file, nothing to stop` and carries on, with no message box and no error.
  - **Identity check, then kill.** Otherwise it runs the new `{tmp}\stop-asset-check.ps1 -PidPath "{tmp}\asset-state.pid"` with `ewWaitUntilTerminated`. The script ships as `Source: "stop-asset-check.ps1"; DestDir: "{tmp}"; Flags: dontcopy` (the pattern of `force-stop-jarvis.ps1`, `Jarvis.iss:112`). One line, `ExtractTemporaryFile('stop-asset-check.ps1');`, is appended to `ExtractInstallerHelpers` (`Jarvis.iss:891–901`), which `InitializeSetup` already calls (`:913`), so the script is there before the wizard starts. The script dot-sources `asset-helper-identity.ps1` from `$PSScriptRoot` and stops the process only if `Test-AnzuAssetHelperIdentity -PidPath <pid file>` returns `ok`: the same six checks as the force-stop spare above (Setup temp dir, pid file format, pid, image name `powershell.exe`, start ticks, exact `-File` and `-PidPath` arguments). There is no substring test on `CommandLine`. A missing pid file or process is exit 2 as before; any failed check is exit 2, and the log names the check.
    It then stops the helper's descendants (each `Win32_Process` whose `ParentProcessId` is the pid and whose `CreationDate` is not earlier than the helper's start), stops the helper with `Stop-Process -Force`, and waits with `Wait-Process -Timeout 10`. Exit codes:
    - `0`: stopped;
    - `2`: nothing to stop (no pid file, process gone, or any identity field differs, i.e. a reused PID; the log line names the field that differed);
    - `1`: still running after 10 s.
    `taskkill /PID … /T` is not used, so a reused PID and its child tree are never touched.
  - **Leftover file.** After the call, whatever the exit code, `KillAssetCheck` deletes `{tmp}\asset-state.pid` if it is still there (a force-stopped helper can't run its `finally`), so a later call in the same run never acts on it.
  - **Exit code `1`.** On Clean, the Clean branch of `NextButtonClick` shows "Setup couldn't stop the installed-models check (pid <n>). Close Setup and try again." and stays on the page (`Result := False`). The guard at the top of the Clean wipe in `PrepareToInstall` returns the same text, so the wipe never starts while the helper may hold a model file open. On Cancel and in `DeinitializeSetup`, it is logged and Setup exits as today.
  It is called:
  - on Clean, before anything is deleted (and again at the top of the Clean wipe in `PrepareToInstall`, as a guard);
  - from a new `CancelButtonClick` handler, when the owner confirms Cancel;
  - at the start of the existing `DeinitializeSetup` (`Jarvis.iss:773`), whose existing lines are unchanged.
  Setup itself never opens a GGUF. Hashing runs only in that child PowerShell process (read-only, `FileShare.Read`), so once the child is gone no handle is held and the Clean wipe can delete every file.
- **Timeout or failure: visible fallback, never a silent block or skip.** The overall timeout is 300 s from launch. On timeout, an `{"error"}` result, unparsable JSON, or a failed `Exec`, Setup kills the helper (`KillAssetCheck`) and logs the reason to the Setup log and `installer-assets.log`. Then:
  - **Ordinary model rows** are left **unticked and enabled**, with S3's and S4's labels not applied, so nothing downloads unless the owner ticks it.
  - **Successor rows** are **disabled and unticked**, with the suffix "(update check unavailable)". **Which rows (D2 sixth review #2): a static list built in at compile time, never the detection that just failed.** On every existing install that reaches the fallback, whatever is installed, the rows are the tasks of every catalogue component that is the `superseded_by` target of any component in `installer/windows/model-catalog.json`. `[Code]` doesn't read the catalogue at run time. `installer/windows/gen_model_catalog_iss.py` (new, S3) writes `installer/windows/model-catalog.generated.iss` (new, committed) from the catalogue, and `Jarvis.iss` includes it with one `#include "model-catalog.generated.iss"` line at the top of `[Code]`. For S3 that file holds one constant: `const CatalogSuccessorTasks = 'dl_localllm';`, the comma-separated Inno task names (each catalogue component gets a `task` field naming its `[Tasks]` entry, e.g. `fable_9b` → `dl_localllm`). On this RFC's catalogue the list is exactly `dl_localllm`, the `fable_9b` target of Ornith and Abiray. The fallback (`ApplyAssetFallback`) reads only that constant, with no file read, no JSON and no detection variable, so it is the same after a timeout before any marker was read. A drift test regenerates the include and compares it byte for byte. **Decision: disable, not "unticked with the `(can be updated to …)` label".** That label needs S3's ±25 % profile comparison and the installed-version read, both of which came from the run that failed, so showing it would be a guess. An enabled row without the label would offer a ~6 GB model switch the owner can't see. Disabling means the successor is never offered silently and never mislabelled, and the next Update offers it properly. `/UPGRADEMODELS=fable_9b` in silent mode still works, because that is an explicit opt-in.
  - The task page shows the note "Couldn't check installed models (<reason>). Nothing is pre-selected; tick what you want, and Setup will verify each file before downloading it. Model updates can't be offered this time." The Finished page repeats it.
  - `AssetNeedsCopy(component, destPath)` falls back to **S1's file-exists check**: true only when `not FileExists(destPath)`, the same test S1's `ExistingFable9BMissing` uses; for a wildcard component's marker it also compares the marker's `version` ("Version marker for wildcard payloads" below). So a present ~6 GB Fable is not re-copied when the check fails. `bootstrap.ps1` still runs `Get-AnzuAssetState` per file at install time, so a present, unchanged file is not downloaded again either.
- **Silent mode** (`/SILENT` and `/VERYSILENT`; D2 sixth review #3). The launch is the same `ewNoWait` launch in `InitializeWizard`. The wait can't sit in `NextButtonClick` or `CurPageChanged`:
  - `NextButtonClick` sets `Result := True` and `Exit`s for every page except `ExistingInstallPage` (`Jarvis.iss:1096–1100`);
  - `CurPageChanged` exits at once when `WizardSilent` (`Jarvis.iss:756–757`).
  Both stay unchanged. The hook is `PrepareToInstall` (`Jarvis.iss:1498`), which silent installs reach before any `[Files]` entry (and so any `AssetNeedsCopy` check) is processed. One new block goes after the existing `SelectedAction` assignment (`:1520–1523`) and before `if SelectedAction <= 2 then` (`:1524`), and no existing line moves: `if WizardSilent and AssetCheckLaunched and not AssetStateApplied then begin if SelectedAction = 3 then KillAssetCheck else AwaitAssetStateSilently; end;`. `AwaitAssetStateSilently` behaves as follows:
  - **Result already written:** it is applied at once.
  - **Check still running:** it waits with `Sleep(250)` until the result file appears or the 300 s budget runs out. The budget is **measured from the `InitializeWizard` launch**: there is no second launch and no fresh budget. Each new progress line goes to the Setup log as `asset check: <component> <file> <percent>`. `/VERYSILENT` shows nothing; `/SILENT` shows Inno's own "Preparing to install" progress window while it waits.
  - **On a result:** it fills the state `AssetNeedsCopy` and the `/UPDATE` refresh read. No task list is touched, because no page is shown, and successors are installed only when `/UPGRADEMODELS` names them.
  - **On timeout, `{"error"}`, or unparsable JSON:** it runs `KillAssetCheck`, then the same fallback, which logs "Couldn't check installed models (<reason>)…". `AssetNeedsCopy` falls back to S1's `FileExists`, and there is no successor without `/UPGRADEMODELS`. The install continues: this block never sets `PrepareToInstall`'s `Result`, so a silent install never aborts because of the check.
  - **In every case** it sets `AssetStateApplied`.
  Interactive installs reach `PrepareToInstall` with `AssetStateApplied` already true, because Next stays disabled on `wpSelectTasks` until the result or the fallback is applied, so the block never runs for them.

**Visible progress.** The inline indicator above shows the helper's `{tmp}\asset-state.progress` lines (`<component> <file> <percent>`); a cache hit shows "verified (cached)". In silent mode the same lines go to the log.

**Interplay with `ShouldCopyDefault9BPayload` (S1/S3).** S4 replaces only the body of S1's `ExistingFable9BMissing` with `AssetNeedsCopy('fable_9b', <Fable dest path>)`, so an own-default repair now also re-copies a damaged or unverifiable Fable, not only a missing one. The fresh-install, Clean-reinstall and opt-in branches are unchanged, and `LmStudioServesFable` still wins. An install whose Fable is present and unchanged copies nothing. With the successor unticked on an Ornith install, `ShouldCopyDefault9BPayload` stays false whatever `asset-state` says.

**Version marker for wildcard payloads (S4; D2 sixth review #4).** On `development` @ `bd2558b` (#661 landed; `Jarvis.iss` unchanged since `a44da353`), the wildcard `Source:` lines in `Jarvis.iss` `[Files]` are:
- `:91–101`, the application trees `android`, `backend`, `config`, `docs`, `frontend`, `installer`, `mcp`, `project`, `scripts`, `tools` and `voice_packs`;
- `:102` `*.md` and `:103` `*.ps1`;
- `:107` `backend\app\runtime\*` and `:108` `frontend\dist\*`;
- `:157` `payload\models\tts\kokoro-82m\*` (`recursesubdirs createallsubdirs`);
- `:163` `payload\desktop\sidecars\*`.

Only `:157` is a model payload. `:163` is the backend sidecar binary, which is application code and must be refreshed on every Upgrade / Update. It and the application trees keep no `Check`, so they are copied as today. The other model payloads are single files: `:153` (front 2B) and S1's Fable line. They pass their own `{app}` file path. So Kokoro is the one wildcard component in this RFC:
- `:157` gains `Check: AssetNeedsCopy('kokoro_82m', ExpandConstant('{app}\models\tts\kokoro-82m\.anzu-asset-version.json'))` and stays inside the existing `#ifndef SkipVoicePack`.
- **Marker path:** `{app}\models\tts\kokoro-82m\.anzu-asset-version.json`. It is not in the payload: no staging script writes it, and no `Source:` names it.
- **Marker contents:** one line of JSON, `{"component":"kokoro_82m","version":"{#AssetVersion_kokoro_82m}","installer_version":"{#MyAppVersion}","written_at":"<yyyy-mm-dd hh:nn:ss>"}`. `AssetVersion_kokoro_82m` is a `#define` that S4 adds to `model-catalog.generated.iss`: the generator emits one `#define AssetVersion_<component> "<catalogue version>"` per wildcard model component.
- **Uninstall (D2 eighth review #2).** `[UninstallDelete]` (`Jarvis.iss:196–203`) gains one line after `:203`: `Type: files; Name: "{app}\models\tts\kokoro-82m\.anzu-asset-version.json"`. The marker is written by `[Code]`, not by `[Files]`, so the uninstaller would otherwise leave it behind. In addition, `AssetNeedsCopy` returns True first, without reading any marker, when `not ExistingInstallDetected` (fresh install). So a fresh install always copies Kokoro, even if an old marker was left behind by a manual delete or a pre-S4 uninstaller. If `{app}\models` survives an uninstall, `DetectExistingInstallation` (`:860`) treats the next run as an existing install: the marker is gone by then, and in JSON mode the Kokoro catalogue files are `missing`, so Kokoro is copied either way.
- **Lifecycle.** In `CurStepChanged(ssInstall)` (before `[Files]` runs), when the memoised decision for `kokoro_82m` is true, the old marker is deleted, so a copy interrupted half-way leaves no marker. In `CurStepChanged(ssPostInstall)`, next to the existing block (`Jarvis.iss:1314–1322`, existing lines unchanged), the marker is written with `SaveStringToFile`, only when this run copied the component. If the write fails, Setup logs it and shows the Finished-page line "Couldn't record the Kokoro voice version; the next Update copies it again." It is never silent.
- **Fallback, version read (D2 eighth review #3).** True (copy) when the marker is missing, or when its `version` differs from the payload version `{#AssetVersion_kokoro_82m}`. The marker is Setup's own fixed-format line, so `[Code]` reads it with `LoadStringFromFile` and takes the value between `"version":"` and the next `"`. A file that doesn't contain that key, or is unreadable, counts as a different version, i.e. copy. So a newer Kokoro payload is copied even when the check fails, and an unchanged one is not.
- **JSON mode.** The helper's per-file size + SHA-256 state for the component's catalogue files decides; it is stronger than the marker. The helper also reads the marker's `version` and reports it as `marker_version` in `asset-state.json` for the log. When the files are verified (a) and the marker is missing or has another version, `ssPostInstall` rewrites the marker, so the fallback's next decision matches the verified files.
- **Payload version = catalogue version.** `stage-voice-default.ps1:58` (`& $Hf download $Repo --local-dir $Payload`) downloads an unpinned revision on `development`. S4 adds `--revision <catalogue kokoro_82m commit>` to that one call, so the staged payload is exactly the catalogue's pinned commit, and `{#AssetVersion_kokoro_82m}` names what is actually shipped. `.jarvis_staged_ok` handling (`:18`, and the write after the download) is unchanged.
- **Why not the existing `.jarvis_staged_ok`:** it sits inside the payload (`stage-voice-default.ps1:18`), so the same wildcard copies it, possibly before the other files, and it carries no version. It stays exactly as it is for its current readers: `bootstrap.ps1:149`, `:590`, `build-installer.ps1:60` and `pack_install.py:231`.
- **Existing installs from before S4** have no marker, so they copy Kokoro once (today's behaviour), and the marker exists from then on.
- **Same pattern for any future wildcard model payload.** A `[Files]` line with `*` under `payload\models\` must pass its `.anzu-asset-version.json`, have a generated `AssetVersion_<component>` define, and be written in `ssPostInstall`. The S4 static test enforces this.

### Stub rule

No stubs. A catalog entry with no SHA, an "Update" option that behaves exactly like Repair, a gate function nobody calls, a migration with no test, or a timer setting that is never read, is a fail.

## Relationship to #648/#649 (landed)

#648 (`d214b6d`) and #649 (`ee786dc`) are on `development`. S2 builds on their code as it is and ports nothing:
- `config.py` `gguf_path`, `_SETTINGS_WRITE_LOCK`, `_saved_snapshot`, `_merge_settings_changes` and the atomic write: S2's new `idle_unload_seconds` is saved through them;
- `manager.py` `_same_endpoint`, `_loaded_profile`, `requested_context_size` and the `_load_locked` cancel/failure cleanup: S2's reload goes through them;
- `hotswap.apply_runtime_profile_to_settings(persist=False)` and the save after a successful load; `api/model.py::load_model`'s `gguf_path` reset;
- `lmstudio_server._loaded_model_ids` (native inventory): S2 reads it to tell idle-unloaded from loaded instances.

Their tests are already on `development` and are not repeated or edited here: `tests/test_rfc0223_startup_model_stability.py` (`test_load_failure_clears_loading_state_and_stale_provider`, `test_endpoint_changes_and_force_do_not_reuse_old_provider`, `test_failed_activation_does_not_replace_saved_selection`, `test_slow_model_selection_and_ui_save_preserve_each_others_changes`, …), `tests/test_profiles.py::test_unloaded_snapshot_uses_profile_context`, `tests/test_inference_backends.py::test_unloaded_snapshot_uses_configured_fast_profile` and `tests/test_runtime_activate.py`. #649's `front_08b` / quick-model pieces and #648's `Jarvis.iss` `Excludes` / `force-stop-jarvis.ps1` changes are unrelated to this RFC; S1/S3/S4 do not touch the `[Files]` `Excludes` lines.

### S4 — Installer skip-unchanged assets (size + SHA-256 against the manifest)

**Model:** Grok 4.6 (fast off) · **Lane:** D2 · **Depends:** S3 (sequential owner of `Jarvis.iss`, `bootstrap.ps1`, `model-catalog.json`, `installed-components.ps1`)

| Path | Why |
| --- | --- |
| `installer/windows/asset-state.ps1` (new) | `Get-AnzuAssetState`: size-first / SHA-256-second check against the catalogue, states `unchanged` / `outdated` / `missing` / `damaged` / `hash-failed`, hash cache, progress file, timeout, visible messages (only owner) |
| `installer/windows/model-catalog.json` | Per-file `size` + `sha256` + `superseded_files[]`; the front 2B constants moved in (third step of the chain S3 → S4) |
| `installer/windows/installed-components.ps1` | Dot-source `asset-state.ps1`; emit `{tmp}\asset-state.json` + progress (second owner after S3) |
| `installer/windows/bootstrap.ps1` | `Ensure-BootstrapGguf` / `Ensure-Front2bGguf` / every model `Ensure-*` call `Get-AnzuAssetState` before downloading; `(already installed)` skip line; damaged / hash-failed lines; the inline `$expectedBytes` is replaced by the catalogue value (third owner: S1 → S3 → S4) |
| `installer/windows/stage-front-model.ps1` | Read `$ExpectedSha` / `$ExpectedBytes` from `model-catalog.json` (only owner in the batch) |
| `installer/windows/stage-voice-default.ps1` | Only: `--revision <catalogue kokoro_82m commit>` on the `hf download` call (`:58`); `.jarvis_staged_ok` unchanged (only owner in the batch) |
| `installer/windows/Jarvis.iss` | Reuses S3's non-blocking run unchanged and adds only: per-file percentages in the indicator text; `AssetNeedsCopy(component, destPath)` (JSON state, falling back to S1's `FileExists` check); `AssetNeedsCopy()` JSON lookup used as `Check:` on the model payload lines (memoised per component; the wildcard Kokoro line `:157` passes its `.anzu-asset-version.json` marker); the Kokoro marker delete in `CurStepChanged(ssInstall)` and write in `CurStepChanged(ssPostInstall)`; the fallback's marker `version` comparison and the fresh-install-first branch of `AssetNeedsCopy`; the `[UninstallDelete]` marker line; `ExistingFable9BMissing` body → `AssetNeedsCopy('fable_9b', <Fable dest path>)`; `(already installed) ` prefix + pre-check on (a) rows; Finished-page summary of damaged / hash-failed lines; no hash logic in Pascal (third owner: S1 → S3 → S4) |
| `installer/windows/gen_model_catalog_iss.py`, `installer/windows/model-catalog.generated.iss` | One `#define AssetVersion_<component>` per wildcard model component (`kokoro_82m`) from the catalogue `version` (second owner after S3) |
| `installer/windows/tests/asset-state.Tests.ps1` (new); `.github/workflows/pr-tests.yml` (one append-only step in the existing Windows `installer-compile` job: `- name: Asset state helper tests (RFC-0228 S4)` / `shell: pwsh` / `run: ./installer/windows/tests/asset-state.Tests.ps1`) | PowerShell behaviour tests (plain asserts, exit 1 on failure; no new module dependency) |
| `tests/test_installer.py`, `tests/test_rfc0228_installer_update.py` | Added tests only (existing tests unchanged) |

**Label rule, add-alongside (S3 behaviour kept).** S3's checked + disabled grey-out and its `(installed)` suffix stay exactly as specified for rows S3 detects as installed by marker or version only, i.e. components with no catalogue `sha256` (some voice packs). S3's `(can be updated to > …)` rows are untouched. S4 only adds: a row whose files were **byte-verified** as (a) is pre-checked and keeps S3's disabled state, and its label carries the `(already installed) ` prefix instead of the `(installed)` suffix, so the same row never says "installed" twice. Nothing is removed from the checklist, Select-all, theming or groups, and fresh installs (no files) see today's labels.

- [ ] **States** (`asset-state.Tests.ps1`, temp tree + fixture catalogue): `unchanged` (exact size + hash) → state (a), no download call, label prefix `(already installed) `, row pre-checked + disabled; `outdated` (matches `superseded_files`) → state (b), S3 label `(can be updated to > …)` unchanged and unchecked; `missing` → state (c), download invoked once; `damaged` (right size, wrong hash; and wrong size) → re-download with "<name> is damaged; downloading it again.".
- [ ] **Size first:** a file whose size matches no catalogue entry is never hashed (hasher call counter = 0).
- [ ] **Hash failure falls back visibly:** locked file (I/O error) and a hasher faked to exceed `-HashTimeoutSeconds 1` → `hash-failed`, download invoked, and "Couldn't verify <name> (<error>); downloading it again." present in `asset-state.json` `message`, in `installer-assets.log` and in the bootstrap log; the run never exits 0 with that line missing.
- [ ] **Cache:** second run on unchanged files → cache hit, hasher not called, progress shows "verified (cached)"; touching the file's mtime or changing its size → miss and re-hash; corrupt cache file → rebuilt with one log line.
- [ ] **Progress:** the progress file receives increasing percentages for a multi-block file; Inno's inline indicator reads it (static).
- [ ] **Runs before Select Tasks:** the mechanism tests are S3's ("Non-blocking detection" in S3). S4 adds, in `tests/test_installer.py`: `test_asset_state_applied_before_tasks_layout` (inside the `wpSelectTasks` branch, `ApplyAssetState` comes before `EnsureSelectAllLayout`, and the existing lines are unchanged); `test_hashing_runs_only_in_child_process` (no `GetSHA256Of*` in `[Code]`; hashing only inside `installed-components.ps1` / `asset-state.ps1`); `test_prepare_to_install_reuses_asset_state_json` (`PrepareToInstall` and `AssetNeedsCopy` only read `{tmp}\asset-state.json`, and `installed-components.ps1` is never run there).
- [ ] **Kill releases the file (`asset-state.Tests.ps1`):** `test kill mid-hash releases the GGUF`: start a hash of a 512 MiB fixture file, run the `KillAssetCheck` command line on the helper's PID, then the file is deleted successfully within 2 s; a second case asserts the helper opened the file read-only with `FileShare.Read`.
- [ ] **Timeout / failure fallback (`asset-state.Tests.ps1` + static):** a helper faked to hang past a 2 s test timeout → killed by PID, the fallback result holds every component as `needs_copy`, the note text "Couldn't check installed models" is in the Setup-log fixture and `installer-assets.log`, and no row is pre-ticked (static: the `ApplyAssetFallback` branch unticks and enables every ordinary model row, disables and unticks successor rows with "(update check unavailable)", and sets the note label), and a present Fable is not re-copied (`AssetNeedsCopy` → `FileExists` fallback). A helper exiting with `{"error": "…"}`, and a truncated JSON file, give the same fallback with their reason. Then `bootstrap.ps1` on a present, unchanged file still skips the download (its own helper call). Silent mode: the same timeout writes the note to the log and the install continues.
- [ ] **One code path (static, `tests/test_installer.py`):** `test_asset_state_helper_is_the_only_hash_path` (`[Code]` of `Jarvis.iss` contains no `GetSHA256OfFile` / `GetSHA256OfStream` / size comparison; `installed-components.ps1` and `bootstrap.ps1` dot-source `asset-state.ps1`; no other installer script calls `Get-FileHash` for a model except `asset-state.ps1`, the existing post-download verifier `front-model-download.ps1:131` and the build-time staging check `stage-front-model.ps1:46`, which now reads its expected values from the catalogue); `test_model_payload_lines_use_asset_needs_copy` (every `[Files]` line sourcing `payload\models\…` carries `AssetNeedsCopy(`. A single-file line passes its own `{app}` file path. A line whose `Source:` contains `*` (today only `:157` Kokoro) passes `{app}\<DestDir>\.anzu-asset-version.json`, its component has an `AssetVersion_<component>` define in `model-catalog.generated.iss`, and `CurStepChanged(ssPostInstall)` writes that marker. `payload\desktop\sidecars\*` (`:163`) and the application trees (`:91–108`) carry no `AssetNeedsCopy`); `test_wildcard_marker_lifecycle` (static: the marker is deleted in `ssInstall` and written in `ssPostInstall` only when the memoised decision is true, its JSON has `component`, `version`, `installer_version` and `written_at`, no staging script writes `.anzu-asset-version.json` and no `Source:` names it, and `.jarvis_staged_ok` handling in `bootstrap.ps1` / `stage-voice-default.ps1` is byte-identical); `test_kokoro_marker_removed_on_uninstall` (static: `[UninstallDelete]` has the `.anzu-asset-version.json` line, and `AssetNeedsCopy`'s first branch returns True on `not ExistingInstallDetected` before any marker read); `test_kokoro_marker_version_compared` (static on the fallback branch, plus a `[Code]`-equivalent fixture table: marker missing → copy; marker `version` equal to `AssetVersion_kokoro_82m` → no copy; marker with another `version` → copy; marker without a `version` key → copy); `test_stage_voice_pinned_to_catalog_revision` (`stage-voice-default.ps1`'s `hf download` passes `--revision` read from `model-catalog.json`); `test_fable_payload_check_still_gated_by_opt_in` (`ShouldCopyDefault9BPayload` still has only the fresh / clean / own-repair / opt-in branches, own-repair now via `AssetNeedsCopy('fable_9b', …)``); `test_catalog_files_have_size_and_sha256` (every catalogue file entry: int `size` > 0, 64-hex `sha256`); `test_front_model_constants_come_from_catalog` (no literal SHA or byte count left in `stage-front-model.ps1` / `bootstrap.ps1`); `test_installer_compile_job_runs_asset_state_tests` (the CI step exists in `installer-compile`).
- [ ] **Labels (`tests/test_rfc0228_installer_update.py`):** `test_unchanged_asset_row_prechecked_with_already_installed_prefix`, `test_outdated_row_keeps_can_be_updated_label`, `test_marker_only_row_keeps_installed_suffix`, `test_missing_row_downloads`.
- [ ] **(D2 eighth review #2, #3) Windows soak `kokoro_marker_roundtrip`:** install, then uninstall: no `.anzu-asset-version.json` and no Kokoro file left. A fresh install then copies Kokoro (the Setup log lists the Kokoro files) and writes the marker with the payload version. Editing the marker's `version` to an older value and running Update with the check forced into the fallback (`asset-state.ps1` renamed) copies Kokoro again and rewrites the marker. With the version unchanged, the same run skips it.
- [ ] Windows soak on Taco's PC: the task page is usable within 2 s on an Update after an Update (cache hit); on a cold cache the indicator shows progress while Back and Cancel stay responsive; Update after an Update → no GGUF downloaded or copied again, verification of ~6 GB served from the cache in under 2 s; renaming one byte of a GGUF → "damaged; downloading it again" shown and the file restored.
- [ ] Inno compile passes in `installer-compile`, with the new step green.

Sequential chains: `config.py` #649 (landed) → 0228-S1 → 0228-S2 → 0231-S2 (#665, RFC-0231, final head in this PR's body; `LargePromptSettings`) → 0233-S1 (#668, RFC-0233, final head in this PR's body; `CapabilityBuildSettings`) → #670 (RFC-0211 port, draft, which supersedes #585; final head in this PR's body; one `testing =` line, lands last) — the same order as the `config.py` rows of RFC-0231 and RFC-0233; `Jarvis.iss` 0228-S1 → 0228-S3 → 0228-S4; `bootstrap.ps1` 0228-S1 → 0228-S3 → 0228-S4; `model-catalog.json` and `installed-components.ps1` 0228-S3 → 0228-S4; `tests/test_rfc0228_installer_update.py` 0228-S3 (creates the file and owns its existing tests) → 0228-S4 (adds only the four label tests, editing none of S3's); `tests/test_installer.py` 0228-S4 only in this RFC (added tests, existing ones unchanged); `asset-state.ps1` and `stage-front-model.ps1` only 0228-S4; `lmstudio_server.py` 0225-S3 → 0228-S2; `manager.py` 0225-S3 → 0228-S2 (two owners); `gen_model_catalog_iss.py` and `model-catalog.generated.iss` 0228-S3 → 0228-S4; `stop-asset-check.ps1`, `asset-helper-identity.ps1`, their tests, the `force-stop-jarvis.ps1` parameter and call, and the `ForceStopJarvisUnder` statement only 0228-S3; `stage-voice-default.ps1` only 0228-S4; `api/model.py` is not edited by this RFC (#648's changes there are landed). **`hotswap.py` has one owner, RFC-0225 S3; no 0228 slice edits it.** `lmstudio_context.py`, `gpu_prefer.py`, `profile_roles.py`, `model_escalation.py` and the new `rewarm.py` are edited only by 0228-S2; **`rewarm.py` has one owner, 0228-S2**. Managed-mode state is owned by RFC-0225 S3 (`engine_coexistence.py`); 0228-S2 only reads it and calls its hooks.

`frontend/package.json` and `.github/workflows/pr-tests.yml` are shared by every frontend ticket in the 2026-10-17 batch: each ticket adds exactly one `test:*` script line and one `frontend-build` step (append-only hunks, trivial rebase) and touches nothing else in those files.

## Out of scope

- Persona/presence/WebGL/appearance (Astra).
- Auto-update channel / background updater service (this is the installer's Update choice).
- Changing the 27B coder or its Ollama model configuration.
- Stopping foreign engines and the VRAM gate itself (RFC-0225).

## Risks

- **HF repo churn** (80+ commits, last updated 2026-10-17) → pin by commit SHA + file SHA256 in `model-catalog.json`.
- **Uncensored default** → consistent with the existing abliterated default and owner decision; policy gates (RFC-0002/0031) unchanged.
- **Fable loses the benchmark** → no default change (gate); S1 reports to the Architect.
- **Reload latency after idle** → visible loading state; owner can set "Never".
- **Driving owner-loaded LM Studio instances** → only with managed mode on (explicit, remembered, revocable consent); reload reuses the owner's recorded model key and context so his setup is restored as it was.
